title: University of Maryland - CS21 Bowtie

question.stem: Complete the diagram by dragging from the choices below to specify what condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take to address that condition, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor to assess the client’s progress.
question.footnote: Taken from the Maryland Next Gen NCLEX Test Bank Project, University of Maryland School of Nursing: “Thyroid Storm” medical-surgical faculty case study, stand-alone bow-tie (Suzana Jarquin, MSN, RN, CNEcl, Frederick Community College, September 1, 2022; updated April 23, 2023). Available at https://www.nursing.umaryland.edu/mnwc/initiatives/nextgen-nclex/nextgen-nclex-library/ (Faculty Case Studies). Laboratory values shown in SI units.
question.preamble: The nurse reviews the client’s laboratory results.
question.explanation:
The client is experiencing a thyroid storm, which requires an antithyroid medication such as methimazole. To decrease the client’s metabolic demands, the nurse promotes a calm, restful environment; cooling measures and IV fluids are also needed. Body temperature and serum thyroid levels are important parameters to monitor.
A warming blanket, levothyroxine, and fluid restriction would worsen the client’s condition. Daily weights, the amount of sleep, and the WBC count are not effective ways to assess this client’s progress.

tabs.title: Nurses' Notes
tabs.content: 0900:Accompanied by spouse; reports being short of breath and having palpitations. Placed in an ED treatment room directly from triage. Alert and oriented × 4; appears restless, anxious, and fatigued. Skin flushed and hot to touch. Bilateral eye protrusion noted; client states this is not their baseline and that their eyes feel “very dry.” Lung sounds clear to auscultation; no cough, but intermittent and worsening dyspnea. Normal S1 and S2; bilateral pulses 2–3+. Hyperactive bowel sounds in all 4 quadrants. Reports no pain. Reports excessive hunger and thirst over the past week, unrelieved by oral intake, and an unexpected weight loss of about 4 kg (8 lb) over the past week.
